note: The U.T. total row of the CEO's table. The Karaikal district total of 1,57,503 agrees with the CEO's part-wise pages for constituencies 24 to 28. The five Karaikal constituency rows of the summary table add to 1,57,236, which is 267 fewer, so those rows lag the part-wise data and the total row is used. From the CEO's press note as India Today NE quotes it: 19,94,357 electors, 9,69,298 men, 10,24,735 women and 324 third gender. The press note itself was not found on ceomanipur.nic.in on 12 November. The report does not say whether service electors are included.

5,77,46,618 electors, 2,82,03,992 men, 2,95,34,734 women and 7,892 third gender, as The South First reported the consolidated draft roll. Dinakaran gives the same figures. No press release on the draft was on elections.tn.gov.in on the evening of 12 November. The report does not give service electors or the names added and deleted since the final roll.

The CEO's figures as Khas Khabar quotes them: 5,26,67,416 electors, 2,75,24,780 men, 2,51,42,052 women and 584 transgender. The report does not say whether the count covers all 200 seats. The final roll it is set against covers 199 seats and leaves out Anta, so the change from it may include Anta's electors. Service electors and the names added and deleted were not given. No press note on the draft was found on election.rajasthan.gov.in.

1,90,16,768 electors, 94,84,635 men, 95,31,721 women and 412 third gender, as Lalluram reports the draft roll. The report does not name the CEO's press note. Service electors and the names added and deleted were not given. No press note on the draft was on ceochhattisgarh.nic.in on the evening of 12 November.

Dainik Bhaskar reports 5,47,99,628 general electors on the draft roll of 12 November, which is 8,18,563 more than the 5,39,81,065 on the final roll of 21 February 2026, and 71,530 service electors (68,978 men and 2,552 women), for 5,48,71,158 in all. It gives the rise as 3,80,169 men and 4,38,361 women, the men and women on the draft only in crore (2.82 and 2.65), and third gender electors as 937 against 904 in February. The 8,18,563 is a net change, and the names added and deleted since February were not reported. The paper also reports 72,036 polling stations after 127 were added and 21 removed, and that claims and objections close on 11 December, are to be decided by 28 December, and the final roll is due on 4 January 2027.

Dainik Jagran reports from the office of the Chief Electoral Officer 7,55,89,365 electors on the draft roll, of whom 3,99,16,747 are men, 3,56,71,129 are women and 1,489 are third gender. The paper sets them beside 7,46,91,135 electors in October 2025, the roll of the Assembly election, which is a rise of 8,98,230. The base in this file is the final roll of the intensive revision of 30 September 2025, so the change of 13,97,008 from it also takes in the 4,98,778 by which the roll grew between that final roll and the roll of the Assembly election of 2025. Hindustan Times on 13 November gives the draft as 75.5 million and about 1.3 million more than the 74.2 million after the intensive revision. No press note on the draft was on ceoelection.bihar.gov.in on 13 November, where the latest press note listed is dated 23 October 2026. Service electors and the names added and deleted since the final roll were not given.

The figures are the total row of the Chief Electoral Officer's summary of the draft electorate. The total of 2,73,60,254 includes 2,45,883 overseas electors, who are 2,06,943 men, 38,931 women and 9 third gender. General electors alone are 2,71,14,371, of whom 1,31,14,324 are men, 1,39,99,787 are women and 260 are third gender. The total with overseas electors is recorded here because the final roll of 21 February 2026 in final.csv counts them too. The CEO's statement as PTI reported it on ThePrint on 12 November gives the same total, men, women, third gender and number of overseas electors. A figure of 2,66,78,256 in a post by The South First on 12 November is not in the CEO's summary and was not used. Service electors and the names added and deleted since the final roll were not given.

From the Chief Electoral Officer's announcement as Pratidin Time reports it: 2,51,76,910 electors on the draft roll, of whom 1,25,87,650 are men, 1,25,88,939 are women and 321 are third gender. The report also gives 63,237 service electors and six overseas electors, and does not say whether the service or overseas electors are in the total. Assam was not in the intensive revision. The roll before this draft is the final roll of Assam's special revision of 10 February 2026, 2,49,58,139 electors, which is the figure the Assam pages carry. The report gives 4,12,344 names added and 1,93,573 deleted since then, a net rise of 2,18,771, and the figures add up for every sex.

From the CEO's press note F.No 16/4/2025-ELC of 12 November 2026, read from the scanned page because its text layer is damaged. The note puts the draft roll as on 12.11.2026 at 57,701 electors, 29,273 men, 28,428 women and no third gender electors. It says 639 of them are aged 18 or 19. It gives no count of service electors and no count of names added or deleted since the final roll of 14 February 2026.

The figures are those the Additional Chief Electoral Officer, Dr Vijay Kumar Jogdande, gave to the press, as Dainik Jagran and Aaj Tak reported them on 13 November 2026. The two reports agree on every figure. The draft roll holds 72,78,035 general electors, 37,93,373 men, 34,84,447 women and 215 third gender electors. Both reports give 86,028 service electors in addition, 83,352 men and 2,676 women, and the men, women and third gender add to the total without them. Names of 1,25,216 electors were added in a special campaign from 4 to 31 October 2026. The reports say 6,130 applications in Form 7 to delete names were decided, and they do not say how many names were deleted. The final roll of 3 October 2026 held 71,58,949 electors, and 71,58,949 plus 1,25,216 less 6,130 equals the draft exactly, which would be so if every one of those applications ended in a deletion. A second Jagran report gives the change since the final roll as 63,411 men and 55,672 women, and the two rolls give 55,672 more men and 63,411 more women, so that report has the two figures the wrong way round. The CEO's own press note on the draft was not on ceo.uk.gov.in on 14 November 2026, where the latest press note listed is of 22 October.
